collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — DEPARTURES AND EXILE (DEP-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Leaving and being left: moving huts, short journeys, visitors going home, goodbyes done well and badly, homesickness, and the rare person who sails away for good. Choosing to leave is never a rejection of one's people, and choosing to stay is never a failure.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: A villager who dreams of living alone on a tiny island paddles out to try it: stay until sunset, or come back for dinner.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: Out past the reef there is a tiny island, just a few palms and a beach, close enough to see but far enough to need a canoe. (name1) has always dreamed of living there by (him/her)self, in a little hut, fishing and thinking and talking to nobody. Today (he/she) paddles out for an afternoon to see what it's like.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: After an hour, (name1) has seen everything there is to see. Twice. The palms are nice. The beach is nice. It is extremely quiet. (He/she) paddles home in time for dinner, a little puzzled. (He/she) might go back. It was lovely. It was also lonely in a way (he/she) hadn't expected, and (he/she) is still thinking about that.

o1__fx.name: Outcome A
o1__fx.text: (name1) stays all afternoon. (He/she) swims, sleeps, eats a coconut and walks round the whole island eleven times. At sunset (he/she) watches the village lights come on across the water, small and warm. (He/she) paddles back in the dusk. (He/she) still wants the little island. Just not every day.
